rationale:
Split. The supplied proof of PolyhedralApproximation (Simon 6.2) has two logically independent halves joined by a short diagonal argument.

(I) Printed first paragraph. For finite-mass integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, the scaled deformation theorem gives lattice chains Pc with |X(ω) − Pc(ω)| ≤ Cρ(M(X)‖dω‖ + M(∂X)‖ω‖).

(II) Printed second paragraph. The truncations T⌞{φ>λ} by an exhaustion function have finite boundary mass for a.e. λ by slicing (4.5). They are integer multiplicity with compact support and extend to ℝ^{n+ℓ}.

Half (II) rests on the facts the supplied proof collects as (P1)–(P3): representation and restriction of currents, restriction of τ(M,θ,ξ), and extension. These are genuine, reusable results of Simon §1–§3 and can be proved independently. Children:
- finite_mass_approximation: (I) plus the ρ_k choice of Step 5. Needs DeformationTheorem.
- truncation_sequence: (II), i.e. Steps 1–3 plus the choice of λ_k. Needs SlicingTheorem and three siblings.
- restriction_exists (P1, Simon 2.9): T⌞A exists, and every restriction has locally finite mass.
- restriction_tau (P1/P2): every restriction of τ(M,θ,ξ) to A is τ(M∩A,θ,ξ), i.e. it does not depend on the representation.
- open_truncation (P2+P3): for V ⊂⊂ U, τ(M∩V,θ,ξ) is an integer multiplicity current on ℝ^P of finite mass.
- pairing_expansion (Simon 1.5–1.7 coordinates): ⟨c,w⟩ = Σ_I c_I⟨dx^I,w⟩ and |c_I| ≤ |c|. Used by three siblings.
- measure_uniqueness: signed measures on U are determined by C_c^∞(U). This is the analytic core of restriction_tau.

DeformationTheorem and SlicingTheorem are siblings of the selected node, not of these children. The two children that need them therefore take them as explicit hypotheses. The parent discharges these with its declared dependencies, Submission.deformation_theorem and Submission.slicing_theorem.

Assembly (supplied Steps 5–6 and P4):
1. truncation_sequence gives X_k ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}), integer multiplicity, with M(X_k)+M(∂X_k) < ∞ and X_k(ω) = T(ω) eventually, for each ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U).
2. finite_mass_approximation applied to (X_k) gives positive antitone ρ → 0, integer β, and Pc_k with Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0.
3. Set P_k := (Pc_k).restrictDomain (subset_univ U). IsLatticeChain (ρ k) (β k) P_k holds because restriction does not change the underlying form.
4. P_k(ω) = (Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)) + X_k(ω) → T(ω).
This assembly compiles in Lean; #print axioms reports [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

One deviation from the supplied text keeps to the printed proof. The supplied proof truncated by T⌞{φ ≥ λ} with f = φ and needed the density argument of its (P2) at points of {φ = λ}. The printed proof uses T_λ = T⌞{φ > λ}, and truncation_sequence follows that choice. It obtains ∂(T⌞{φ>λ}) from the frozen SlicingTheorem with f = −φ and t = −λ, since {−φ < −λ} = {φ > λ}; this is 4.7 up to sign. For the open set {φ > λ}, the weighted tangent planes of M and M∩{φ>λ} agree at every point of {φ>λ}. That is a local statement, so no density theorem is needed. This locality step is kernel-checked against the SimonGMT definitions. Admissible λ still form a full-measure subset of each interval (1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)).

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of the n-vector/n-covector pairing (Simon 1.5–1.7)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-vector w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (a continuous linear functional on n-covectors, `NVector`) and every n-covector c ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) (a continuous alternating map, `Covector`): w(c) = Σ_I c_I · w(dx^I), where I ranges over the strictly increasing multi-indices Fin n ↪o Fin P (`SimonMultiIndex n P`), c_I := c(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)}) (`euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I`) and dx^I := dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n−1)} (`wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))`). Moreover |c_I| ≤ |c| for every I, where |c| is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm (`covectorEuclideanNorm c`).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n) (c : Covector (Eucl P) n), w c = ∑ I : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I * w (wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j))) ∧ ∀ I : SimonMultiIndex n P, |euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For k ∈ Fin P let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 be the standard basis; EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k = e_k (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). An n-covector is a continuous alternating map c : Eⁿ → ℝ (Covector E n). An n-vector w is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (NVector E n). For J : Fin n → Fin P write e_J := (e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(n−1)}). For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, i.e. an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P (a strictly increasing map), put c_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate c I = c(e_I) and dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)).

1. (dx^I on increasing basis tuples.) By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for every J : Fin n → Fin P, dx^I(e_J) = det(Matrix.of fun i j => proj_{I(i)}(e_{J(j)})) = det[δ_{I(i),J(j)}]_{i,j}.
   - If J = ⇑I, the matrix is the identity, so dx^I(e_I) = 1.
   - If J = ⇑I′ for some I′ ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P with I′ ≠ I, then range I ≠ range I′. Indeed, a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the unique order embedding onto its range, so it is determined by its range. Both ranges have exactly n elements, so some I(i) ∉ range I′. Row i of the matrix is then zero, and dx^I(e_{I′}) = 0.
   Hence dx^I(e_{I′}) = 1 if I′ = I and 0 otherwise.
2. (Sorting injective tuples.) Let J : Fin n → Fin P be injective and s := range J, a Finset of card n. Let I_J := s.orderEmbOfFin (card s = n) ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P be the increasing enumeration of s (Finset.orderEmbOfFin); then range I_J = s. Since I_J is a bijection Fin n → s and J takes values in s, σ := I_J⁻¹ ∘ J is a permutation of Fin n with J = I_J ∘ σ. For every alternating map α on Eⁿ, AlternatingMap.map_perm gives α(e_J) = α(e_{I_J} ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·α(e_{I_J}).
3. (c = Σ_I c_I dx^I.) Let c′ := Σ_I c_I·dx^I ∈ Covector E n.
   - For I′ ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, step 1 gives c′(e_{I′}) = Σ_I c_I·[I = I′] = c_{I′} = c(e_{I′}).
   - For injective J, step 2 applied to c′ and to c gives c′(e_J) = sign(σ)·c′(e_{I_J}) = sign(σ)·c(e_{I_J}) = c(e_J).
   - By Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the underlying alternating maps and the standard basis of E, two alternating maps that agree on all tuples of pairwise distinct basis vectors are equal. Hence c′ = c as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ext).
   - Degenerate cases are included. For n > P there is no injective J and no I, and both c and c′ are 0. For n = 0 there is exactly one I (the empty embedding), dx^∅ is the constant covector 1, and c = c(∅)·1.
4. (Pairing.) w is linear, so w(c) = w(Σ_I c_I·dx^I) = Σ_I c_I·w(dx^I) (map_sum, map_smul). This is the first conjunct.
5. (Coordinate bound.) By definition covectorEuclideanNorm c = √S, where S := Σ_{J : Fin n → Fin P} (if StrictMono J then c(fun i => basisFun (J i))² else 0) is a sum of nonnegative terms. For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, ⇑I is StrictMono and basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i) = e_{I(i)}, so the summand for J = ⇑I equals c_I². Hence c_I² ≤ S (Finset.single_le_sum), and |c_I| = √(c_I²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm c (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). This is the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^I(e_{I′}) = δ_{I,I′} for increasing I, I′, from the determinant formula wedgeCovectors_apply_det.
Every injective basis tuple is a permutation of an increasing one: α(e_J) = sign σ · α(e_{I_J}).
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives c = Σ_I c_I dx^I.
Linearity of w gives w(c) = Σ_I c_I w(dx^I).
c_I² is one nonnegative summand of covectorEuclideanNorm(c)², so |c_I| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm c.

subproblems.title: Signed measures on an open set are determined by smooth test functions
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let μ₁, μ₂ be Borel measures on ℝ^P and g₁, g₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ functions such that g_i is μ_i-integrable on every compact K ⊆ U. Suppose ∫ ψ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ ψ g₂ dμ₂ for every C^∞ function ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ U. Then ∫_A u g₁ dμ₁ = ∫_A u g₂ dμ₂ for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P and every continuous u : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport u ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl P)) (g₁ g₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn g₁ K μ₁ ∧ IntegrableOn g₂ K μ₂) → (∀ ψ : Eucl P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ U → ∫ x, ψ x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, ψ x * g₂ x ∂μ₂) → ∀ A : Set (Eucl P), MeasurableSet A → ∀ u : Eucl P → ℝ, Continuous u → HasCompactSupport u → tsupport u ⊆ U → ∫ x in A, u x * g₁ x ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in A, u x * g₂ x ∂μ₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the uniqueness half of Simon's representation (2.7) used for the restriction (2.9) in the supplied proof's (P1): the signed Radon measures g₁μ₁⌞U and g₂μ₂⌞U agree on C_c^∞(U), hence agree. Note that ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) is C^∞ (it is definitionally ContDiff ℝ ∞ with the ContDiff notation).

1. (Localization.) Fix A and u, and let K := tsupport u, a compact subset of U.
   - If K = ∅, then u ≡ 0 and both sides vanish. Assume K ≠ ∅.
   - By IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open there is r > 0 with L := cthickening (2r) K ⊆ U. L is closed and bounded, hence compact.
   - O := thickening r K is open with K ⊆ O ⊆ L. Every function that vanishes outside K, or outside O, vanishes outside L.
2. (Finite measures.) For i = 1, 2, g_i is μ_i-integrable on L, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for μ_i⌞L. Fix a Borel function h_i with h_i = g_i μ_i⌞L-a.e.
   - Define ν_i⁺ := (μ_i⌞L).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(h_i x)) and ν_i⁻ := (μ_i⌞L).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(−h_i x)).
   - They are finite, since ν_i^±(ℝ^P) ≤ ∫_L |g_i| dμ_i < ∞.
   - Put λ₁ := ν₁⁺ + ν₂⁻ and λ₂ := ν₂⁺ + ν₁⁻; both are finite Borel measures.
3. (Integrals against λ_i.) Let b : ℝ^P → ℝ be bounded and Borel.
   - Integration against a finite-valued measurable density gives ∫ b dν_i^± = ∫_L b·h_i^± dμ_i, all finite, where h⁺ = max(h,0) and h⁻ = max(−h,0).
   - Since h_i⁺ − h_i⁻ = h_i = g_i μ_i⌞L-a.e., we get (★): ∫ b dλ₁ − ∫ b dλ₂ = ∫_L b g₁ dμ₁ − ∫_L b g₂ dμ₂.
4. (Agreement on smooth functions supported in O.) Let ψ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O.
   - Then tsupport ψ ⊆ U, so the hypothesis gives ∫ ψ g₁ dμ₁ = ∫ ψ g₂ dμ₂.
   - ψ vanishes outside O ⊆ L, so ψ g_i = 1_L ψ g_i and ∫ ψ g_i dμ_i = ∫_L ψ g_i dμ_i.
   - By (★) with b = ψ, ∫ ψ dλ₁ = ∫ ψ dλ₂.
5. (Radon–Nikodym.) Let ν := λ₁ + λ₂, a finite measure. Then λ_i ≪ ν.
   - With f_i := (x ↦ (λ_i.rnDeriv ν x).toReal), f_i is ν-integrable and ∫ b dλ_i = ∫ b f_i dν for every bounded Borel b (integral_rnDeriv_smul).
   - By step 4, ∫ ψ·(f₁ − f₂) dν = 0 for every C^∞ ψ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O.
   - f₁ − f₂ is ν-integrable, hence locally integrable on O. By IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero, applied to the open set O, f₁ = f₂ ν-a.e. on O.
6. (Conclusion.) b := 1_A·u is bounded, Borel, and vanishes outside K ⊆ O.
   - Hence b f₁ = b f₂ ν-a.e., and ∫ b dλ₁ = ∫ b f₁ dν = ∫ b f₂ dν = ∫ b dλ₂.
   - By (★), ∫_L 1_A u g₁ dμ₁ = ∫_L 1_A u g₂ dμ₂.
   - Since u = 0 outside K ⊆ L, the μ_i-integrable function 1_A u g_i vanishes outside L, so ∫_L 1_A u g_i dμ_i = ∫_A u g_i dμ_i.
   Therefore ∫_A u g₁ dμ₁ = ∫_A u g₂ dμ₂. ∎
proof_key_steps: Localize: K = tsupport u, compact L = cthickening(2r) K ⊆ U, open O = thickening r K.
Finite measures λ₁ = g₁⁺μ₁⌞L + g₂⁻μ₂⌞L and λ₂ = g₂⁺μ₂⌞L + g₁⁻μ₁⌞L with identity (★).
λ₁ and λ₂ agree on smooth functions supported in O.
Radon–Nikodym w.r.t. λ₁+λ₂ and IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero: densities agree a.e. on O.
Integrate 1_A·u against λ₁, λ₂ and unwind (★).

subproblems.title: Restrictions T⌞A exist and have locally finite mass (Simon 2.9)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and T ∈ D_n(U).
(a) Let (μ, v) be a measure representation of T (IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v: for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), ⟨ω,v⟩ is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫⟨ω,v⟩ dμ), and let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then there is S ∈ D_n(U) with IsRestriction T A S.
(b) If A ⊆ ℝ^P and S ∈ D_n(U) satisfy IsRestriction T A S, then M_W(S) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → ∀ A : Set (Eucl P), MeasurableSet A → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsRestriction T A S) ∧ ∀ (A : Set (Eucl P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsRestriction T A S → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), CompactlyContainedOpen W U → S.massOn W < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the supplied proof's (P1) for the restriction X⌞A(ω) := ∫_A⟨ω, X⃗⟩ dμ_X (Simon 2.9), for an arbitrary representation (2.7).

Notation. For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P let dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)), a fixed n-covector. For an n-covector α let α_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I, let |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, and let ‖α‖ be its operator norm. Let N be the number of elements of SimonMultiIndex n P.

1. (Norm comparison.) For every α, |α_I| = |α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_j ‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖. The sum defining |α|² has nonzero terms only for strictly increasing J : Fin n → Fin P, which correspond bijectively to SimonMultiIndex n P. Hence |α| ≤ √N·‖α‖.
2. (Cut-offs.) Let K ⊆ U be compact.
   - By IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open choose r > 0 with cthickening (2r) K ⊆ U.
   - Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma (exists_contMDiffMap_zero_one_of_isClosed, model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ∞) to the disjoint closed sets ℝ^P ∖ thickening r K and K. This gives a C^∞ function χ_K : ℝ^P → [0,1] with χ_K = 1 on K and χ_K = 0 off thickening r K.
   - Then tsupport χ_K ⊆ cthickening r K ⊆ U, which is compact.
   - For each I, the form x ↦ χ_K(x)·dx^I is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ⊆ U, so it belongs to Dⁿ(U).
3. (Local integrability of coordinates.) Let (μ, v) be any representation of T and g^I(x) := v(x)(dx^I). Fix a compact K ⊆ U.
   - By the representation property, x ↦ v(x)(χ_K(x)·dx^I) = χ_K(x)·g^I(x) is μ-integrable.
   - This function coincides with g^I on the Borel (closed) set K, so g^I is μ-integrable on K.
   - Hence G := Σ_I |g^I| is μ-integrable on K.
4. (Pointwise bound.) By pairing_expansion, for all x and all n-covectors α, v(x)(α) = Σ_I α_I·g^I(x) and |α_I| ≤ |α|. Hence |v(x)(α)| ≤ |α|·G(x).
5. (Existence, (a).) Fix (μ, v) and a Borel set A. For ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) set S(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x).
   - Linearity: each integrand is μ-integrable on ℝ^P, hence on A, so S is ℝ-linear (linearity of the integral and of each v(x)).
   - Sequential continuity: let ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j, and the 0-th derivatives converge uniformly on K. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. As ω_j = 0 off K, steps 1 and 4 give |S(ω_j)| ≤ ∫_K |v(x)(ω_j(x))| dμ ≤ √N·ε_j·∫_K G dμ → 0.
   - So S is a GeometricCurrentOn U n. IsRestriction T A S holds by construction: A is measurable and S(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω,v⟩ dμ with the representation (μ, v).
6. (Finiteness, (b).) Suppose IsRestriction T A S. Then A is Borel and S(ω) = ∫_A v′(x)(ω(x)) dμ′(x) for some representation (μ′, v′) of T.
   - Let W ⊂⊂ U and K := closure W, compact with K ⊆ U. By step 3 for (μ′, v′), G′ := Σ_I |v′(·)(dx^I)| is μ′-integrable on K.
   - Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) be admissible for M_W, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U n W).
   - Then v′(x)(ω(x)) = 0 for x ∉ K, and |v′(x)(ω(x))| ≤ G′(x) by step 4. Hence S(ω) ≤ ∫_A |v′(ω)| dμ′ ≤ ∫_K G′ dμ′ =: c_W < ∞.
   - Therefore M_W(S) = sup ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ ofReal(c_W) < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Covector norm comparison: |α_I| ≤ ‖α‖, so covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ √N ‖α‖.
Smooth cut-offs χ_K make χ_K·dx^I test forms; the coordinates v(·)(dx^I) are integrable on compact K ⊆ U.
pairing_expansion: |v(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(α)·Σ_I |v(x)(dx^I)|.
S(ω) := ∫_A ⟨ω,v⟩ dμ is linear and sequentially continuous, hence a current with IsRestriction T A S.
Any restriction satisfies S(ω) ≤ ∫_{closure W} Σ_I |v′^I| dμ′ for admissible ω, so M_W(S) < ∞.

subproblems.title: Restriction of τ(M,θ,ξ) to a Borel set A is τ(M∩A,θ,ξ)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ D_n(U), and let (M, θ, ξ) be a rectifiable triple in U (IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ) with T(ω) = τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ (tauAction n M θ ξ ω) for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(U). If A ⊆ ℝ^P and S ∈ D_n(U) satisfy IsRestriction T A S, then S(ω) = ∫_{M∩A} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = tauAction n (M ∩ A) θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → ∀ (A : Set (Eucl P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsRestriction T A S → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = tauAction n (M ∩ A) θ ξ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the supplied proof's (P1)/(P2): the restriction T⌞A does not depend on the representation, and for T = τ(M,θ,ξ) it equals τ(M∩A,θ,ξ).

Notation. dx^I, α_I and χ_K are as follows. For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) and α_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I. For compact K ⊆ U, χ_K is a C^∞ function ℝ^P → [0,1] with compact support, tsupport χ_K ⊆ U and χ_K = 1 on K. It is obtained by choosing r > 0 with cthickening (2r) K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and applying the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contMDiffMap_zero_one_of_isClosed to the closed sets ℝ^P ∖ thickening r K and K. Write Hⁿ := μHE[n] and ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M.

Unpack IsRestriction T A S: A is Borel, and there is a representation (μ, v) of T (IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v) with S(ω) = ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).

1. (Unit simple n-vectors.) By the orientation field of the triple, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ for an orthonormal τ. simpleNVector τ is built by mkContinuous with bound Π_i |τ_i| = 1, so ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1. Hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for ν-a.e. x and all n-covectors α.
2. (Coordinate functions.) For each I put g₁^I(x) := v(x)(dx^I) and g₂^I(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(dx^I).
   (a) g₁^I is μ-integrable on every compact K ⊆ U. The test form χ_K·dx^I ∈ Dⁿ(U) makes x ↦ χ_K(x)·g₁^I(x) μ-integrable, and this function equals g₁^I on K.
   (b) g₂^I is ν-integrable on every compact K ⊆ U. Here ν⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) since K is Borel. θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K (triple field integrableOn). The function x ↦ ξ(x)(dx^I) is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (ξ is, and evaluation at a fixed covector is continuous linear) and bounded by ‖dx^I‖ a.e. by step 1. Hence the product is integrable.
3. (Agreement on smooth functions.) Let ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ U.
   - Then ω_ψ := (x ↦ ψ(x)·dx^I) lies in Dⁿ(U), with v(x)(ω_ψ(x)) = ψ(x)·g₁^I(x) and θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω_ψ(x)) = ψ(x)·g₂^I(x).
   - By the representation and the τ formula for T: ∫ ψ g₁^I dμ = T(ω_ψ) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω_ψ) dHⁿ = ∫ ψ g₂^I dν.
4. (Uniqueness.) Apply measure_uniqueness with U, μ₁ := μ, μ₂ := ν, g₁ := g₁^I and g₂ := g₂^I; its hypotheses hold by steps 2 and 3. Hence for every Borel A′ and every continuous u with compact support and tsupport u ⊆ U, ∫_{A′} u g₁^I dμ = ∫_{A′} u g₂^I dν.
5. (Coordinates of ω.) Fix ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and put u_I(x) := (ω(x))_I = ω(x)(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)}).
   - u_I is continuous, because ω is continuous and evaluation at a fixed tuple is continuous linear on covectors.
   - u_I vanishes wherever ω vanishes, so it has compact support with tsupport u_I ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ U.
   - Step 4 with A′ := A gives ∫_A u_I g₁^I dμ = ∫_A u_I g₂^I dν.
6. (Expansion.) By pairing_expansion with c = ω(x), applied to w = v(x) and to w = ξ(x) (then multiplied by θ(x)), for every x: v(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I u_I(x) g₁^I(x) and θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I u_I(x) g₂^I(x). Each u_I g_i^I is integrable on A: u_I is bounded and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ U, on which g_i^I is integrable by step 2.
7. (Conclusion.) Using steps 5 and 6 and finite additivity of the integral:
   S(ω) = ∫_A v(ω) dμ = Σ_I ∫_A u_I g₁^I dμ = Σ_I ∫_A u_I g₂^I dν = ∫_A θ ξ(ω) dν.
   Since A is measurable, ν⌞A = Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence ∫_A θ ξ(ω) dν = ∫_{M∩A} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = tauAction n (M ∩ A) θ ξ ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsRestriction: S(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω,v⟩ dμ for some representation (μ,v) of T.
Coordinate functions g₁^I = v(·)(dx^I) w.r.t. μ and g₂^I = θ ξ(·)(dx^I) w.r.t. Hⁿ⌞M are locally integrable on U (‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 a.e.).
Both pair with smooth ψ to T(ψ dx^I).
measure_uniqueness: ∫_A u g₁^I dμ = ∫_A u g₂^I d(Hⁿ⌞M) for continuous compactly supported u.
Expand ω in coordinates (pairing_expansion), sum over I, and use (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞A = Hⁿ⌞(M∩A).

subproblems.title: τ(M∩V,θ,ξ) for V ⊂⊂ U is an integer multiplicity current on ℝ^P of finite mass
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, V, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for all x ∈ M. Suppose V ⊂⊂ U, i.e. V is open, closure V is compact and closure V ⊆ U. Then there is an integer multiplicity current X ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) with M(X) < ∞ and X(ω) = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = tauAction n (M ∩ V) θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ x ∈ M, ∃ k : ℕ, θ x = k) → CompactlyContainedOpen V U → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, IsIntegerMultiplicity X ∧ X.mass < ∞ ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n, X ω = tauAction n (M ∩ V) θ ξ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the supplied proof's (P2)+(P3) for an open truncation set: X is T⌞V for T = τ(M,θ,ξ), extended to ℝ^P, as for the printed T_λ = T⌞{φ > λ}.

Let N := closure V (compact, N ⊆ U), M′ := M ∩ V and Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P let dx^I := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)). For an n-covector α let α_I := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. (Integrability of θ.) By the triple field integrableOn with K = N, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ N. Since M′ ⊆ M ∩ N, θ is integrable on M′ and on M′ ∩ K for every set K. In particular θ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M′. Put Θ := ∫_{M′} θ dHⁿ < ∞.
2. (Bounds for ξ.) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, and ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π_i |τ_i| = 1 (mkContinuous bound). Hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all n-covectors α. Moreover, by pairing_expansion (ξ(x)(α) = Σ_I α_I ξ(x)(dx^I) and |α_I| ≤ |α|), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ c_*·|α| for a.e. x ∈ M, where c_* := Σ_I ‖dx^I‖.
3. (The functional.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P) and F_ω(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)).
   - F_ω is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M′: θ is by step 1, and x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) composes the a.e.-strongly measurable pair (ξ, ω) with the continuous evaluation map.
   - |F_ω| ≤ θ·sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ a.e. on M′ by step 2; the supremum is finite because ω is continuous with compact support.
   - Hence F_ω is Hⁿ⌞M′-integrable. Define X(ω) := ∫_{M′} F_ω dHⁿ = tauAction n M′ θ ξ ω.
   - X is linear, by linearity of each ξ(x) and of the integral of integrable functions.
4. (Continuity.) Let ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(ℝ^P), i.e. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 for the domain univ. All tsupports lie in one compact K, and ω_j → 0 uniformly on K (0-th derivative; ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖). So ε_j := sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0, and |X(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·Θ → 0 by step 2. Hence X ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) (a GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and X(ω) = tauAction n (M ∩ V) θ ξ ω for all ω.
5. (Finite mass.) If ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P) has |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, then by step 2, X(ω) ≤ ∫_{M′} θ·|ξ(ω)| dHⁿ ≤ c_*·Θ. Hence M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X) ≤ ofReal(c_*Θ) < ∞.
6. (Tangent planes are local.) Claim: if x ∈ V and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q, then HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ x Q.
   - The dimension condition finrank Q = n is unchanged.
   - Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Choose R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open).
   - Let 0 < r < δ/R, η := blowUpMap x r (y ↦ r⁻¹(y − x)), g(y) := f(y)·θ(x + r•y) and B := B̄_R(0), a closed Borel set.
   - f vanishes off B, so g = 1_B·g. By setIntegral_indicator (which needs only B measurable), ∫_{η(M)} g dHⁿ = ∫_{η(M)∩B} g dHⁿ, and likewise for M′.
   - η(M) ∩ B = η(M′) ∩ B. Indeed, if y = η(z) with z ∈ M and |y| ≤ R, then |z − x| = r|y| ≤ rR < δ, so z ∈ V and z ∈ M′. The other inclusion is clear.
   - Hence the integrals of Simon's Definition 1.7 for M and for M′ coincide for every r ∈ (0, δ/R), a set in 𝓝[>] 0. So they have the same limit θ(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ (Tendsto.congr′).
   - This step has been kernel-checked against the SimonGMT definitions.
7. (Integer multiplicity.) The triple (M′, θ, ξ) satisfies IsRectifiableTriple univ n M′ θ ξ:
   - M′ ⊆ ℝ^P.
   - M′ = M ∩ V is Hⁿ-null-measurable, because M is and V is open.
   - M′ is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono, M′ ⊆ M).
   - θ > 0 on M′ ⊆ M.
   - θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M′ ∩ K for every compact K (step 1).
   - ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M′, the restriction of Hⁿ⌞M to a subset (mono_measure).
   - Orientation: Hⁿ⌞M′ ≤ Hⁿ⌞M, so for Hⁿ⌞M′-a.e. x we have x ∈ M′ (ae_restrict_mem₀ with null-measurability) and the orientation property of (M,θ,ξ) holds. That is, there is an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. Since x ∈ V, step 6 gives the tangent condition for M′.
   Finally θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M′ ⊆ M, and X(ω) = tauAction n M′ θ ξ ω for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P). Hence X is integer multiplicity, witnessed by the triple (M ∩ V, θ, ξ), and M(X) < ∞ by step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ is integrable on M ∩ closure V; ξ is a.e. a unit simple n-vector (‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1).
X(ω) := ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear and sequentially continuous on Dⁿ(ℝ^P).
pairing_expansion gives |⟨α,ξ(x)⟩| ≤ (Σ_I ‖dx^I‖)·covectorEuclideanNorm α, so M(X) < ∞.
For x in the open set V, weighted tangent planes of M and M∩V coincide (blow-ups agree on supp f for small r).
(M∩V, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P with θ ∈ ℕ, so X is integer multiplicity.

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity truncations T⌞{φ>λ_k} with finite mass and boundary mass (Simon 6.2, second paragraph)
subproblems.lean_statement: SlicingTheorem → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → T.massOn W < ∞ ∧ T.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → ∃ X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1), (∀ k, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X k)) ∧ (∀ k, (X k).mass + (X k).boundary.mass < ∞) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), ∀ᶠ k in atTop, X k (testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) (m + 1) ω) = T ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 6.2, second paragraph of the printed proof (p. 169), with Steps 1–3 and the λ-choice of Step 5 of the supplied parent proof. The printed proof takes a Lipschitz φ with φ > 0 in U, φ ≡ 0 off U and {φ > λ} ⊂⊂ U. For L¹-a.e. λ > 0, 4.5 gives T_λ ≡ T⌞{φ > λ} with M(∂T_λ) < ∞; since spt T_λ ⊂ U, the finite-mass case applies (errata: ‘ans’ = and, ‘{x D φ(x) > λ}’ = {x : φ(x) > λ}). We truncate exactly as printed, by the open sets {φ > λ}. The frozen SlicingTheorem describes ⟨T,f,t⟩ = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} (4.6). We apply it with f = −φ and t = −λ, so {f < t} = {φ > λ}; this is 4.7 up to sign. The supplied proof's variant T⌞{φ ≥ λ} would need its density argument (P2) at points of {φ = λ}. With the open set {φ > λ}, the tangent condition is local (sibling open_truncation).

Notation. n := m + 1; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; W ⊂⊂ U means CompactlyContainedOpen W U. A test form ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) is regarded as an element of Dⁿ(ℝ^P) via testFormOnInclusion, which does not change the underlying form.

0. (Representation.) T is integer multiplicity, so there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M, and T(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(U). In particular M ⊆ U.
1. (Exhaustion function.) If U = ℝ^P let φ(x) := 1/(1+|x|). Otherwise let φ(x) := min{dist(x, ℝ^P∖U), 1/(1+|x|)}, using Metric.infDist; this case includes U = ∅, where φ ≡ 0.
   (a) φ is 1-Lipschitz on ℝ^P. x ↦ dist(x,F) is 1-Lipschitz (lipschitz_infDist_pt). For a, b ≥ 0, |1/(1+a) − 1/(1+b)| = |a−b|/((1+a)(1+b)) ≤ |a−b|, and ||x| − |y|| ≤ |x−y|. A minimum of 1-Lipschitz functions is 1-Lipschitz.
   (b) For t > 0, K_t := {x : φ(x) ≥ t} is compact and K_t ⊆ U. It is closed because φ is continuous, and contained in the closed ball of radius 1/t. If U ≠ ℝ^P and x ∈ K_t, then dist(x, ℝ^P∖U) ≥ t > 0, while dist(y, ℝ^P∖U) = 0 for y ∉ U; so x ∈ U.
   (c) φ > 0 on U. If U ≠ ℝ^P, then ℝ^P∖U is closed and nonempty, so dist(x, ℝ^P∖U) > 0 for x ∈ U (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). Consequently, for every compact K ⊆ U there is δ > 0 with φ ≥ δ on K: this is trivial for K = ∅, and otherwise the continuous φ attains a positive minimum on K.
   For t > 0 put V_t := {x : φ(x) > t}. It is open with closure V_t ⊆ K_t, so V_t ⊂⊂ U and V_t ⊆ U.
2. (Slices.) f := −φ is 1-Lipschitz on U. Apply SlicingTheorem to P, m, U, T, f and L = 1; its hypotheses are ours. We get S : ℝ → D_m(U) such that (i) IsSlice T f s (S s) for every s ∈ ℝ, and (iv) the mass bound holds.
   - By (i), for each s there are A_s ∈ Dⁿ(U) and B_s ∈ D_m(U) with IsRestriction T {x ∈ U : f(x) < s} A_s and IsRestriction ∂T {x ∈ U : f(x) < s} B_s.
   - Also S_s(ψ) = ∂A_s(ψ) − B_s(ψ) = A_s(dψ) − B_s(ψ) for ψ ∈ D^m(U).
   - Note {x ∈ U : f(x) < −λ} = U ∩ V_λ.
   - Unpacking IsRestriction for s = 0 gives a measure representation (μ, v) of T (IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v).
3. (Choice of levels.) Fix k ∈ ℕ. Put a := −1/(k+1) < b := −1/(k+2) and W_k := V_{1/(2(k+2))}; W_k is open, W_k ⊆ U and W_k ⊂⊂ U by step 1.
   - E_k := {x ∈ U : a < f(x) < b} is Borel (U open, f continuous).
   - By restriction_exists (a) with (μ, v) there is R_k with IsRestriction T E_k R_k. By restriction_exists (b), M_{W_k}(R_k) < ∞.
   - f is 1-Lipschitz on ℝ^P, so ‖fderiv ℝ f x‖ ≤ 1 for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence L_W := 1 satisfies the a.e. derivative hypothesis on W_k.
   - The mass bound of SlicingTheorem (for W_k, L_W = 1, a < b and R_k) gives a measurable g_k : ℝ → [0,∞] with M_{W_k}(S_s) ≤ g_k(s) for s ∈ (a,b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g_k ≤ M_{W_k}(R_k) < ∞.
   - Hence g_k < ∞ for L¹-a.e. s ∈ (a,b) (ae_lt_top for the restricted measure). Since L¹((a,b)) = b − a > 0, there is s_k ∈ (a,b) with g_k(s_k) < ∞, i.e. M_{W_k}(S_{s_k}) < ∞.
   - Put λ_k := −s_k, so 1/(k+2) < λ_k < 1/(k+1).
4. (Truncated currents.) For each k apply open_truncation to (M, θ, ξ), U and V := V_{λ_k} ⊂⊂ U. This gives an integer multiplicity X_k ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P) with M(X_k) < ∞ and X_k(η) = tauAction n (M ∩ V_{λ_k}) θ ξ η = ∫_{M∩V_{λ_k}} θ⟨η,ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every η ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^P). (X_k is the printed T_{λ_k} = T⌞{φ > λ_k}, extended to ℝ^P.)
5. (Finite boundary mass.) Fix k and write λ := λ_k, s := s_k = −λ, A := A_s, B := B_s, S := S_s and W := W_k.
   (a) Apply restriction_tau to U, T = τ(M,θ,ξ) and IsRestriction T {x ∈ U : f(x) < s} A. It gives A(η) = tauAction n (M ∩ {x ∈ U : f(x) < s}) θ ξ η for η ∈ Dⁿ(U). Since M ⊆ U, M ∩ {x ∈ U : −φ(x) < −λ} = M ∩ V_λ. Hence A(η) = ∫_{M∩V_λ} θ⟨η,ξ⟩ dHⁿ.
   (b) By restriction_exists (b), applied to the current ∂T ∈ D_m(U) and B, M_W(B) < ∞. By step 3, M_W(S) < ∞.
   (c) (Cut-off.) F₁ := {φ ≥ 3λ/4} and F₀ := {φ ≤ λ/2} are disjoint closed sets.
       - By the smooth Urysohn lemma (exists_contMDiffMap_zero_one_of_isClosed, model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ∞) there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0,1] with χ = 0 on F₀ and χ = 1 on F₁.
       - Then {χ ≠ 0} ⊆ {φ > λ/2}, so tsupport χ ⊆ K_{λ/2}.
       - K_{λ/2} is compact, contained in U, and contained in W because λ/2 > 1/(2(k+2)).
   (d) Let ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) with |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; these are the admissible forms for M(∂X_k) = M_{ℝ^P}(∂X_k). Put ψ′ := χψ (x ↦ χ(x)·ψ(x)).
       - ψ′ is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ′ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ψ′ ∈ D^m(U).
       - By homogeneity of covectorEuclideanNorm, |ψ′(x)| = χ(x)·|ψ(x)| ≤ 1.
       - Hence ψ′ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U m W.
   (e) On the open set O := {φ > 3λ/4} ⊆ F₁ we have ψ′ = ψ.
       - The exterior derivative is computed pointwise from fderiv: extDeriv ω x = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ ω x). fderiv depends only on the germ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). So dψ′ = dψ on O.
       - Since V_λ ⊆ O, the integrands θ(x)⟨dψ(x),ξ(x)⟩ and θ(x)⟨dψ′(x),ξ(x)⟩ agree at every x ∈ M ∩ V_λ.
       - Therefore, by step 4, (a) and IsSlice: ∂X_k(ψ) = X_k(dψ) = ∫_{M∩V_λ} θ⟨dψ,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V_λ} θ⟨dψ′,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = A(dψ′) = S(ψ′) + B(ψ′).
   (f) By (d), ofReal S(ψ′) ≤ M_W(S) and ofReal B(ψ′) ≤ M_W(B) (le_massOn). Hence ofReal ∂X_k(ψ) ≤ ofReal S(ψ′) + ofReal B(ψ′) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(B). Taking the supremum over admissible ψ, M(∂X_k) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(B) < ∞ by (b). With step 4, M(X_k) + M(∂X_k) < ∞.
6. (Eventual agreement.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and K := tsupport ω, compact with K ⊆ U.
   - By step 1(c) choose δ > 0 with φ ≥ δ on K, and k₀ with 1/(k₀+1) < δ.
   - For k ≥ k₀, λ_k < 1/(k+1) ≤ 1/(k₀+1) < δ, so K ⊆ V_{λ_k}.
   - x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x),ξ(x)⟩ vanishes outside K, so it equals 1_{V_{λ_k}}(x)·θ(x)⟨ω(x),ξ(x)⟩ everywhere.
   - By setIntegral_indicator (V_{λ_k} open), X_k(ω) = ∫_{M∩V_{λ_k}} θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHⁿ = T(ω).
   Thus X_k(ω) = T(ω) for all k ≥ k₀, which is the eventual equality. ∎
proof_key_steps: Represent T = τ(M,θ,ξ); build the 1-Lipschitz exhaustion φ with {φ ≥ t} compact in U and V_t = {φ > t} ⊂⊂ U.
Apply SlicingTheorem to f = −φ: IsSlice gives A = T⌞(U∩V_λ), B = (∂T)⌞(U∩V_λ), S = ∂A − B, and a representation of T.
Use restriction_exists to get R_k and finite M_{W_k}(R_k); the slicing mass bound picks λ_k ∈ (1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)) with M_{W_k}(S) < ∞.
open_truncation gives an integer multiplicity X_k = τ(M ∩ V_{λ_k}, θ, ξ) on ℝ^P of finite mass.
Use restriction_tau (A = τ(M∩V_λ)), a smooth cut-off χ, and locality of d: ∂X_k(ψ) = S(χψ) + B(χψ), so M(∂X_k) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(B) < ∞.
For ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ V_{λ_k} eventually, so X_k(ω) = T(ω).

subproblems.title: Lattice-chain approximation of finite-mass integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Simon 6.2, first paragraph)
subproblems.lean_statement: DeformationTheorem → ∀ m ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∀ X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ))) (m + 1), (∀ k, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X k)) → (∀ k, (X k).mass + (X k).boundary.mass < ∞) → ∃ (ρ : ℕ → ℝ) (β : ℕ → LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) (m + 1 + ℓ) → ℤ) (Pc : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ))) (m + 1)), (∀ k, 0 < ρ k) ∧ Antitone ρ ∧ Tendsto ρ atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ (∀ k, IsLatticeChain (ρ k) (fun F => (β k F : ℝ)) (Pc k)) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ))) (m + 1), Tendsto (fun k => Pc k ω - X k ω) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 6.2, first paragraph of the printed proof (p. 169). For any ρ_k ↓ 0, the scaled deformation theorem (with ρ = ρ_k) gives T − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k (printed (1)) with M(R_k) ≤ cρ_k M(T) and M(S_k) ≤ cρ_k M(∂T) (printed (2)). Hence P_k(ω) → T(ω); the printed ‘T_k(ω)’ is a misprint for T(ω), and the printed F_n(ρ_k), β_R^{(k)} mean 𝓛_n(ρ_k), β_F^{(k)}. Here this is applied to a sequence X_k with the mass-dependent choice of ρ_k from Step 5 of the supplied parent proof.

Notation. d := m+1+ℓ, n := m+1. For a j-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and ‖α‖ is the operator norm. M(Y) = M_{ℝ^d}(Y) = Y.massOn univ.

1. (Homogeneity.) For a ∈ ℝ and a j-covector α, |aα| = |a|·|α|: each coordinate (aα)(e_J) equals a·α(e_J), so the sum of squares is multiplied by a², and √(a²s) = |a|√s.
2. (Finite sup norms.) For a strictly increasing J : Fin j → Fin d, |α(e_J)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i ‖e_{J(i)}‖ = ‖α‖. Hence |α| ≤ √N_j·‖α‖, where N_j is the (finite) number of strictly increasing maps Fin j → Fin d.
   - A test form η ∈ D^j(ℝ^d) is continuous with compact support, so sup_x ‖η(x)‖ < ∞ and therefore sup_x |η(x)| < ∞.
   - For ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^d), the form dω underlying exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n ω is again a test form.
   - Fix c₀, c₁ > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c₀ and |dω(x)| ≤ c₁ for all x.
3. (Evaluation bound.) Let Y ∈ D_j(ℝ^d) with M(Y) < ∞, η ∈ D^j(ℝ^d), and c > 0 with |η(x)| ≤ c for all x. By step 1, c⁻¹η ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j univ, so ofReal(Y(c⁻¹η)) ≤ M(Y), i.e. Y(η) ≤ c·M(Y).toReal. Applying this to −η gives |Y(η)| ≤ c·M(Y).toReal.
4. (Scales.) Let a_k := (M(X_k) + M(∂X_k)).toReal ≥ 0; then M(X_k).toReal ≤ a_k and M(∂X_k).toReal ≤ a_k. Define ρ₀ := 1/(1+a₀) and ρ_{k+1} := min{ρ_k, 1/((k+2)(1+a_{k+1}))}.
   - By induction ρ_k > 0.
   - ρ_{k+1} ≤ ρ_k, so ρ is antitone (antitone_nat_of_succ_le).
   - ρ_k ≤ 1/((k+1)(1+a_k)) ≤ 1/(k+1) for all k: for k = 0 by definition, and for k+1 by the second argument of min.
   - Hence ρ_k → 0, by squeezing between 0 and 1/(k+1).
5. (Deformation.) Let C = C(m,ℓ) ∈ ℝ≥0 be the constant that DeformationTheorem provides for m and ℓ (1 ≤ ℓ). For each k apply it to T := X_k (M(X_k) + M(∂X_k) < ∞) and ρ := ρ_k > 0. This gives Pc_k, β′_k : faces → ℝ, R_k ∈ D_{n+1}(ℝ^d) and S_k ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^d) with:
   - IsLatticeChain ρ_k β′_k Pc_k;
   - X_k(ω) − Pc_k(ω) = ∂R_k(ω) + S_k(ω) = R_k(dω) + S_k(ω) for all ω;
   - M(R_k) ≤ C·ρ_k·M(X_k) and M(S_k) ≤ C·ρ_k·M(∂X_k);
   - since X_k is integer multiplicity, for every face F there is an integer equal to β′_k(F).
   Choose β_k(F) ∈ ℤ with β′_k(F) = β_k(F) (Classical.choose). Then IsLatticeChain ρ_k (F ↦ (β_k F : ℝ)) Pc_k is the same statement. Also M(R_k) and M(S_k) are finite, with M(R_k).toReal ≤ Cρ_k·M(X_k).toReal and M(S_k).toReal ≤ Cρ_k·M(∂X_k).toReal.
6. (Convergence.) Fix ω ∈ Dⁿ(ℝ^d) and c₀, c₁ from step 2. Apply step 3 to R_k with dω and c₁, and to S_k with ω and c₀:
   |Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω)| = |R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)| ≤ c₁·M(R_k) + c₀·M(S_k) ≤ Cρ_k·(c₁·M(X_k) + c₀·M(∂X_k)) ≤ C(c₀+c₁)·ρ_k·a_k ≤ C(c₀+c₁)·a_k/((k+1)(1+a_k)) ≤ C(c₀+c₁)/(k+1).
   Hence Pc_k(ω) − X_k(ω) → 0. Together with steps 4 and 5, ρ, β and Pc have all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm is homogeneous, and every test form has a finite Euclidean sup norm.
Evaluation bound |Y(η)| ≤ c·M(Y) when |η| ≤ c, via the admissible form c⁻¹η.
Recursive scales ρ_{k+1} = min(ρ_k, 1/((k+2)(1+a_{k+1}))): positive, antitone, ρ_k ≤ 1/(k+1).
DeformationTheorem at scale ρ_k: X_k − Pc_k = ∂R_k + S_k with mass bounds and integer β (by choice).
